messages.author: e5ff05958bd1f6bd
messages.subject: Demote to Integer?
parts:
Hi all, 
I'd like to estimate models describing the colonization of the Pacific. (I've coded my own sampler in C, but STAN's performance and ease-of-use is very appealing, great work!) The trouble is the time frame from which I construct a for loop depends on estimated parameters themselves. Since I can't convert real values to integers I can't execute the for loop, I'm stuck. Here's the model with the diagnostic error message:

model {
    real maxtime; // temp variable for end of time frame
    real mintime; // temp variable for start of time frame
        z ~ normal(0,10) T[0,];  // 
        for (j in 1:ntime) time[j] ~ normal( mu[j] , sigma[j]) T[0,]; 
        maxtime <- round( max( time ) );
    mintime <- round( min( time ) ) + 1;
        for (t in mintime:maxtime ){ // over time
           for ( j in 1:ntime ){ // go through each island for time t
            C <- 0;
            for( k in 1:ntime ){ // go through potential colonizers
            if( time[k]<t ){
            A <- z * access[ k, j ]; // accessibility
            C <- C + A; // update sum
            }
            }
        time[j] ~ bernoulli( 1 - exp( -C ) );
          }
        }
    }

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'model_ILM' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=19, column=18

        for (t in mintime:maxtime ){ // over time
                 ^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
expression denoting integer required; found type=real
Parser expecting: <range expression pair, colon>


I realize the rstan manual states that real values are never demoted to integers. Is there a work-around or am I missing something?

Thanks!
Adrian

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Demote to Integer?
parts:
Does it work if you declare maxtime and mintime as integers instead of reals, as in?

model {
  int maxtime;
  int mintime;
...

There is a difficulty in any model that involves rounding real numbers to integers in that the partial derivative of the rounded number with respect to any parameter it is a function of will be zero. And a HMC model needs the information in the gradient to decide in which direction and how far away to propose a new parameter vector. Also, rounding induces discontinuities, which can undermine the efficiency of the sampler. So, although I think it is possible to make legal Stan syntax out of your model, the results may not be as good as one might hope.

Ben

messages.author: e5ff05958bd1f6bd
messages.subject: Re: Demote to Integer?
parts:
Sorry, my original code was written specifying maxtime and mintime as integers, as you indicated above. Didn't run.

Thanks for bringing up the possible problem with rounding parameters to be integers. With a basic MH sampler I wrote, I ran some analyses fitting simulated data (same model) and it worked great, recovering "true" parameter distributions. Of course, I had to manually tune the step sizes to get the sampler to mix well. I suspect HMC in STAN would do better at tuning than my manual efforts!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Demote to Integer?
parts:
You can fake a for loop with a while loop where you utilize your own counter.

real i;
i = 1;
while(i < maxtime) {
  // stuff
  i++;
}

Ben
